answer: A live-puzzle signing mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to solve a fresh random challenge at task-release time and sign the answer before any reward unlocks. Because the challenge appears only briefly, a farmer running many hollow clones cannot precompute or share responses; each clone needs its own signer, secure keys, and online presence, so costs scale linearly with fake identities. When two submissions show identical patterns, like twin willow branches from one root, both bonds are slashed and burned to a last ember of reputation, making cloning uneconomical.
